quote.text: Among US polymer technician programs (polymer CIP codes) with more than ten lifetime completions, 20 of 73 reported a completion in 2023, or 27%, against 48% for polymer degrees and for six peer trades (IPEDS).

notes.completion: A program on this page is substantive if it recorded more than ten lifetime completions, and active if it reported one in the latest year.

plant.text: Before you count on a local polymer program for hires, check that it still confers: counting degree and technician programs together, Ohio has held 22 with more than ten lifetime completions, and 11 were still conferring in 2023, a different 22 from the technician records in the Ohio table.
Expect most new polymer graduates from Akron to hold graduate degrees: of its 44 completions in the selected codes in 2023, 42 were graduate degrees, master’s or doctorates.

claims.text: Among substantive programs (more than ten lifetime completions), 20 of 73 polymer technician records were active in 2023 (27%), versus 37 of 77 degree records and 3,185 of 6,648 peer-trade records (48% each). Active means a reported completion in 2023. These shares do not establish closure or stability.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census (IPEDS 1991-2023, 2020 dropped as the mirror's duplicate and 2022 (C2023_A) not yet added, see prog-not-recomputed) plus control_cips.json: same rule, same years, same certificate canonicalisation on both sides; polymer CIP codes
claims.assert: D['layers']['technician']['survive_pct'] == 27 and D['layers']['degree']['survive_pct'] == 48 and D['layers']['control']['survive_pct'] == 48 and D['layers']['technician']['survive_pct'] < D['layers']['control']['survive_pct'] and (D['layers']['technician']['still'], D['layers']['technician']['ever']) == (20, 73) and (D['layers']['degree']['still'], D['layers']['degree']['ever']) == (37, 77) and (D['layers']['control']['still'], D['layers']['control']['ever']) == (3185, 6648)
claims.actual: {k: (v['still'], v['ever'], v['survive_pct']) for k, v in D['layers'].items() if isinstance(v, dict)}
claims.falsified_if: Any named numerator or denominator changes, or the technician share ceases to be lower than either comparator. All three must retain the greater-than-ten threshold, positive final-year completion test, certificate canonicalisation and the same years (the mirror's, without 2022: adding C2023_A per program can only raise every numerator and denominator here, so the shares can move either way). These administrative-record shares do not establish a causal difference or stability.
claims.breaks_if: Revised filings put technician programs level with, or above, degrees or peer trades.
claims.guards: Polymer technician programs were less likely to report completions in 2023 than degrees or the peer trades.

counts.noun: more than ten recorded lifetime completions

claims.text: US polymer completions ran 476 in 1991, fell to a floor of 379 in 2007, more than doubled to a 970 peak in 2016, and were 617 in 2023, which is 36% below peak. They fell in five of the seven years since the peak, each compared with the year before it.
claims.source: IPEDS completions, three polymer CIP codes, all award levels, via the Urban Institute API, with the mirror's 2021 and 2022 re-filed to 2020 and 2021 and 2022 taken from NCES C2023_A (_data/build/ipeds_mirror_fix.py, programs_mirror_patch.py)
claims.assert: (D['marks']['first']['year'], D['marks']['first']['awards']) == (1991, 476) and (D['marks']['trough']['year'], D['marks']['trough']['awards']) == (2007, 379) and (D['marks']['peak']['year'], D['marks']['peak']['awards']) == (2016, 970) and (D['marks']['latest']['year'], D['marks']['latest']['awards']) == (2023, 617) and D['marks']['pct_off_peak'] == 36 and D['down_years_last7'] == 5 and D['down_years_of'] == 7 and [r['year'] for r in D['series']] == list(range(1991, 2024))
claims.falsified_if: IPEDS revises a back year, 2024 arrives and extends the series, or the trough flips back to 2006, which sits one completion higher at 380: the two years are a near-tie and an earlier telling named the wrong one. Before 2 November 2026 this said four of five comparable years, because the mirror's late 2021 and 2022 labels stood in for 2020 and 2021 and 2022 was missing; if the mirror reloads, ipeds_mirror_fix.py --check moves these years again and that is a correction, not a quiet re-count.

claims.text: Of 168 polymer technician records since 1991, 95 (57%) are small: ten or fewer recorded lifetime completions. 91 (54%) are brief: first-to-last reporting span of five years or less, inclusive. 75 (45%) satisfy both. These overlapping measures do not establish failed programs.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census, associate and certificate levels, no size threshold, 2020 dropped as the mirror's duplicate and 2022 (C2023_A) not yet added, see prog-not-recomputed; polymer CIP codes; IPEDS 1991–2023
claims.assert: D['base']['ever'] == 168 and D['base']['le10_awards'] == 95 and D['base']['le5_years'] == 91 and D['base']['both'] == 75 and D['base']['both_pct'] == 45
claims.falsified_if: Any named numerator or denominator changes under a source revision, certificate recode or recovered year. The small threshold includes exactly ten; brief measures inclusive calendar span, not count of positive years. Missing source years can change threshold membership and add records to the denominator, so the shares are not failure probabilities or guaranteed bounds on a complete census.

claims.text: Of 8,736 peer-trade technician records, 2,051 (23%) are small, 2,967 (34%) brief, and 1,693 (19%) both. Polymer's small-record share is about 2.4 times the peer-trade share; the small-and-brief ratio is about 2.3. Both ratios use unrounded count-based shares and compare record size and duration. All six trades have lower small and small-and-brief shares separately. The 2023 active-share comparison uses an earlier pull with the same rule; matching rounded rates do not make the two snapshots identical.
claims.source: _data/build/fetch_ipeds_control_baserate.py — the same Urban Institute completions-cip-6 endpoint, the same six CIP codes, the same 1991–2023 span, the same certificate canonicalisation, the same 2020 quarantine, and the size threshold OFF on both sides
claims.assert: (lambda C: C['ever'] == 8736 and (C['le10_awards'], C['le10_awards_pct']) == (2051, 23) and (C['le5_years'], C['le5_years_pct']) == (2967, 34) and (C['both'], C['both_pct']) == (1693, 19) and C['ratio_le10'] == round((D['base']['le10_awards'] / D['base']['ever']) / (C['le10_awards'] / C['ever']), 2) and C['ratio_both'] == round((D['base']['both'] / D['base']['ever']) / (C['both'] / C['ever']), 2) and len(C['per_cip']) == 6 and all(sum(v[k] for v in C['per_cip'].values()) == C[k] for k in ('ever', 'le10_awards', 'le5_years', 'both')) and all(v['le10_awards'] / v['ever'] < D['base']['le10_awards'] / D['base']['ever'] and v['both'] / v['ever'] < D['base']['both'] / D['base']['ever'] for v in C['per_cip'].values()) and C['reproduces']['refetched_survive_pct'] == C['reproduces']['published_survive_pct'] == D['layers']['control']['survive_pct'])(D['layers']['control']['base'])
claims.actual: {k: v for k, v in D['layers']['control']['base'].items() if k not in ('per_cip', 'rule', 'bound')}
claims.falsified_if: Any named count, share or ratio changes, a pooled count differs from its six components, or a peer field's small or small-and-brief share exceeds polymer's. Ratios must divide unrounded shares, each with its own all-record denominator; integer-rounded percentages are display labels. The two populations use different pull dates as well as different size filters: reproducing a rounded 48% does not prove identical counts or source completeness. Missingness may affect fields differently; a shared mirror does not guarantee that the ratio is unchanged.

claims.text: Of Ohio's 22 technician records, 13 have ten or fewer lifetime completions, including one at exactly ten. Two Akron records total nine completions. The size measure does not establish separate failed attempts or current capacity.
claims.assert: D['ohio']['tech_ever'] == 22 and D['ohio']['never_took_off'] == 13 and sum(1 for p in D['ohio']['programs'] if p['total_awards'] <= 10) == 13 and any(p['total_awards'] == 10 for p in D['ohio']['programs']) and sum(1 for p in D['ohio']['programs'] if p['total_awards'] <= 10 and 'AKRON MAIN' in p['institution'].upper()) == 2 and sum(p['total_awards'] for p in D['ohio']['programs'] if p['total_awards'] <= 10 and 'AKRON MAIN' in p['institution'].upper()) == 9
claims.actual: [(p['institution'], p['total_awards']) for p in D['ohio']['programs'] if p['total_awards'] <= 10]
claims.falsified_if: A late completion pushes any of the 13 over ten (the record is live at the bottom: one graduating class changes membership), or a catalogue check shows one of the 13 running substantively under a code this census cannot see — the 'ended is not closed' trap applies to small programs hardest.

claims.text: Ferris State's technician program conferred 1,253 completions across 32 counted years between 1991 and 2023 and is still active, more than the next two programs combined. The record does not yet hold its 2022, so the total is a floor.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census, on the mirror's labels and without C2023_A (see prog-not-recomputed)
claims.assert: (lambda t: 'FERRIS' in t[0]['institution'].upper() and t[0]['total_awards'] == 1253 and (t[0]['first_year'], t[0]['last_year']) == (1991, 2023) and t[0]['status'] == 'active' and t[0]['total_awards'] > t[1]['total_awards'] + t[2]['total_awards'])(D['top_tech'])
claims.actual: [(t['institution'], t['total_awards'], t['status']) for t in D['top_tech'][:3]]
claims.falsified_if: Ferris stops conferring, so status leaves 'active'; a revision breaks the 1991 to 2023 run; or the next two programs' combined total passes 1,253, and Everett and Hennepin are both active and gaining. The span is 32 counted years, not 33: 2022, which the federal mirror never served, is not yet in the per-program record (until 2 November 2026 the missing year was named as 2020), so the lifetime total is a floor.

claims.text: Terra State's associate degree ran 25 unbroken years, 1991–2015, conferred 206 completions, and has filed none since — the largest stopped record at a college that still operates. (Akron Machining Institute's 347 is larger, but the institution itself wound down.)
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census; closure verified against Terra State's current catalogue (narrowed to a single certificate)
claims.assert: (lambda t: t['total_awards'] == 206 and (t['first_year'], t['last_year']) == (1991, 2015) and t['status'] == 'ended')(one(t for t in D['top_tech'] if 'TERRA' in t['institution'].upper())) and one(t for t in D['top_tech'] if 'MACHINING' in t['institution'].upper())['total_awards'] == 347
claims.actual: [(t['institution'], t['total_awards'], t['first_year'], t['last_year'], t['status']) for t in D['top_tech'] if t['status'] != 'active']
claims.falsified_if: Terra State resumes conferring under this CIP (the college still runs one certificate — a revival is possible and would be the better story), or a larger ended program surfaces at an operating college. Separately: Terra State entered state fiscal watch in March 2026 (Auditor of State letter 17 March, ODHE Directive 2026-009 of 23 March), which is a fact about the college, not this record.

claims.text: Akron completions in the three selected polymer codes fell from 114 in 2016 to 44 in 2023 (61%). Graduate degrees supplied 42 of the 44: master's 16, doctorates 26. The bachelor's count was two, within a zero-to-three range across every year 2016–2023. Master's degrees account for 50 of the 70-completion decline and doctorates 19.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census, unitid 200800, with the mirror's years re-filed and 2022 from NCES C2023_A; polymer CIP codes; IPEDS
claims.falsified_if: A revision moves any year, or 2024 arrives. Until 2 November 2026 the 2020 slot was None (the mirror's duplicated year); it is now the mirror's own 2021 row, filed a year late, and 2022 comes from NCES C2023_A, where Akron's bachelor's count is a filed zero.

claims.text: Ohio has held more substantive polymer programs than any state — 22 ever, 11 still conferring in 2023. Substantive means more than ten lifetime completions, at every award level, degree and technician together; this is a different 22 from the 22 technician records in the Ohio table, 13 of which have ten or fewer completions and so are outside this count (plant box; since 2026-11-01 the box says so, after it printed this 22 in words a reader would take for the table's).
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census, substantive programs by state
claims.assert: D['states'][0]['state'] == 'OH' and D['states'][0]['ever'] == 22 and D['states'][0]['still'] == 11 and D['ohio']['tech_ever'] == 22 and D['ohio']['never_took_off'] == 13
claims.falsified_if: Pennsylvania (20 ever) closes the gap in a revision, or the substantive threshold changes. This claim is about filings under polymer CIPs: a state ranking low teaches polymers under codes this census cannot see, so the ranking supports 'Ohio files the most polymer-coded programs', never 'other states lack polymer education'.

claims.text: The Scorecard publishes polymer engineering bachelor's earnings at exactly five institutions — none in Ohio. Their medians run $60k–$78k one year out and $87,636–$100,428 four years out, with median federal-loan debt of $19k–$27k. Four of the five fall below the $92,919 national median for this program code four years out (paytitle h2); the one that clears it, in the data, is University of Massachusetts-Lowell. The page names it in the lede's list but does not single it out.
claims.source: College Scorecard field-of-study files, CIP 14.32, latest vintages (2020 earnings-1yr, 2022 earnings-4yr, 2019 debt)
claims.assert: sorted(r['institution'] for r in D['pay']) == ['Pennsylvania College of Technology', 'Pennsylvania State University-Penn State Erie-Behrend College', 'University of Massachusetts-Lowell', 'University of Wisconsin-Stout', 'Western Washington University'] and all(r['earn_1yr'] and r['earn_4yr'] and r['debt'] and r['earn_4yr_national'] for r in D['pay']) and len(D['pay']) == 5 and all(r['state'] != 'OH' for r in D['pay']) and all(60000 <= r['earn_1yr'] <= 78000 for r in D['pay'] if r['earn_1yr']) and all(87000 <= r['earn_4yr'] <= 101000 for r in D['pay'] if r['earn_4yr']) and all(19000 <= r['debt'] <= 27000 for r in D['pay'] if r['debt']) and min(r['earn_4yr'] for r in D['pay']) == 87636 and max(r['earn_4yr'] for r in D['pay']) == 100428 and all(r['earn_4yr_national'] == 92919 for r in D['pay']) and sum(r['earn_4yr'] < r['earn_4yr_national'] for r in D['pay']) == 4 and one(r for r in D['pay'] if r['earn_4yr'] >= r['earn_4yr_national'])['institution'] == 'University of Massachusetts-Lowell'
claims.actual: [(r['institution'], r['earn_1yr'], r['earn_4yr'], r['earn_4yr_national'], r['debt']) for r in D['pay']]
claims.falsified_if: A new Scorecard vintage unsuppresses a sixth institution (Akron's cells appearing would be the more interesting story), or any value leaves its band. The five are the complete published record because suppression tracks program size — they are the biggest programs, not a sample, and no average of them describes the field. Added 2026-09-28: also fails if the printed endpoints ($87,636/$100,428), the national benchmark ($92,919) or the four-below-median count drift, since the h2 now states those instead of calling the record 'strong'. Extended 2026-09-28: any of the five rows losing an earnings or debt figure fails it; the range bounds used to skip blank rows, so a suppressed value would have passed silently. Extended 2026-09-28 (round 4): the five rows must be the five institutions the lede names, each once; a duplicated row passed the count.

claims.text: This dataset contains no verified example of a substantial polymer technician program dying and being rebuilt. The one candidate dissolved on inspection into a federal reporting change at a continuously running program.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db STORY-SPEC.md Act 4 (the retraction): the Wichita State 'rebuild' was the 2020 certificate-level recode splitting one continuous program into an apparent death and an apparent birth; verified same unitid, unbroken teaching
claims.checked_by: Codex (2026-09-08) re-read the held STORY-SPEC.md retraction. This verifies the recorded candidate's withdrawal, not a universal absence of rebuilds or a fresh catalogue survey.
claims.falsified_if: Someone identifies a program that conferred substantively, stopped for two or more real years (not a code change), and returned to substantive conferral. Finding one would IMPROVE PIC's position — it would be the existence proof the rebuild argument currently lacks.
